trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down, up, left or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going left would force the line onto number 5 before its turn. So the line goes right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6). So my guess (down from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,5); going to number 2, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (up from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try left.
Going left would force the line onto number 5 before its turn; going down would leave both number 5 and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going up, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,6). So the line goes right.
Going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,4). So the line goes right.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
The line must go down: up is number 10, which comes later.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left would leave both cell (5,4) and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes right.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
